template_name: EU AI Act Article 73 — Serious Incident Reporting

provisions.description: A 'serious incident' is an incident or malfunctioning of an AI system that directly or indirectly leads to (a) the death of a person or serious harm to a person's health; (b) a serious and irreversible disruption of the management or operation of critical infrastructure; (c) the infringement of obligations under Union law intended to protect fundamental rights; or (d) serious harm to property or the environment. 'Widespread infringement' is a SEPARATE Art. 73(3) trigger — defined in Article 3, point (61), as an act or omission contrary to Union law protecting individuals' interests that harms, or is likely to harm, the collective interests of individuals residing in at least two Member States — NOT a sub-type or modifier of the 3(49)(c) fundamental-rights trigger. Art. 73(3) sets the 2-day clock for 'a widespread infringement OR a serious incident as defined in Article 3, point (49)(b)' (two independent triggers). The 3(49) triggers form an array because one incident can satisfy several at once (e.g. death and critical-infrastructure disruption).

sub_provisions.description: Death of a person OR serious harm to a person's health. The 10-day clock applies to death only (death_involved=true); non-fatal serious-health-harm uses the 15-day default.
Serious and irreversible disruption of the management or operation of critical infrastructure — 2-day clock.

Infringement of Union-law obligations protecting fundamental rights (Art. 3(49)(c)). NOTE: 'widespread infringement' (Art. 73(3); defined in Art. 3, point (61)) is an INDEPENDENT trigger, NOT a modifier of this one — a 3(49)(c) incident alone takes the general 15-day clock, whereas a widespread infringement (whether or not it is also a 3(49)(c) case) takes 2 days under Art. 73(3).
Serious harm to property or the environment — 15-day default clock.

provisions.retention_years_basis: INFERRED default, NOT stated by Art. 73 (which sets no incident-report retention period). The 10-year figure is the Art. 18 retention for technical documentation / QMS records (Arts. 11/17) and the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), applied here as a defensible practitioner default for the incident record set; it is a profile choice, not a citation of Art. 73 (PhD-review finding 22).
provisions.evaluation_dsl_note: HONESTY CORRECTION (roborev/codex). The Art. 3(49) trigger facts are reachable on EITHER the public card (incident_card.taxonomy_crosswalk.eu_ai_act, §5.5) OR the CONFIDENTIAL source-backed path (incident_report.card_source.eu_ai_act_facts, §5.7). The ACEF generic rule DSL has NO rule-level OR combinator and NO array-element scan, so the EITHER/OR is NOT expressible as a generic DSL rule. The earlier encoding used the vacuous-truth of the UNIVERSAL field_present operator (one rule per record_type, each passing vacuously when no record of that type exists) — but that is WORSE THAN NOTHING: an EMPTY bundle (no incident evidence at all) passes BOTH rules vacuously, giving a FALSE GREEN, and field_present also accepts an empty trigger array. Those vacuous field_present pairs are therefore REMOVED. The existential 'at least one valid evidence path carries the trigger facts' enforcement is DELEGATED to the validator (F-M3-VALIDATOR-RULES, assertion VAL-CLOCK-001), which reads the §5.7 dual fact-source paths and raises ACEF-084 on a clock mismatch — see the article-73 provision's validator_delegated_enforcement block. This provision now retains ONLY rules the DSL can CORRECTLY enforce as per-record conditionals: an advisory has_record_type for the public card (warning — it MUST NOT fail-block the confidential path) and a per-record edition pin (exists_where, advisory).

evaluation.message: A public incident_card is the published Art. 73 surface; on the CONFIDENTIAL source-backed path (§5.7) a RESERVED-id incident_report with card_source and NO public card is fully valid, so this is advisory not binding

When a public incident_card is present, its eu_ai_act crosswalk member should pin edition 'reg-2024-1689' so the trigger codes resolve to the enacted Art. 3(49) text (advisory: existential, only evaluated against cards that exist — the confidential card_source path carries no public card)

When a source-backed incident_report.card_source is present, its eu_ai_act_facts should pin edition 'reg-2024-1689' so the trigger codes resolve to the enacted Art. 3(49) text (advisory: existential, only evaluated against reports that exist)

provisions.description: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market-surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred, immediately after establishing a causal link (or its reasonable likelihood) between the AI system and the incident, and in any event no later than the period set by Art. 73(2)-(4). The reporting clock is the SHORTEST applicable clock over the Art. 3(49) trigger array plus the 'widespread' modifier and the 'death_involved' fact: death_involved -> 10 days; 3.49.b (critical infrastructure) OR widespread -> 2 days; otherwise (including non-fatal 3.49.a serious-health-harm) -> 15 days. Per-provision effective dates carry the Digital-Omnibus 'pending-final-adoption' deferral (Annex III 2027-12-02, Annex I 2028-08-02) while the as-enacted in-force date remains 2026-08-02.

sub_provisions.description: General reporting deadline: no later than 15 days after the provider (or, where applicable, the deployer) becomes aware of the serious incident.

In the event of a widespread infringement or a serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure (Art. 3(49)(b)), the report shall be provided immediately and no later than 2 days after awareness.

In the event of the death of a person, the report shall be provided immediately and no later than 10 days after the date on which the provider (or deployer) became aware of, or has reason to believe, the causal link to the AI system.

provisions.retention_years_basis: INFERRED default, NOT stated by Art. 73 (which sets no incident-report retention period). The 10-year figure is the Art. 18 retention for technical documentation / QMS records (Arts. 11/17) and the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), applied here as a defensible practitioner default for the incident record set; it is a profile choice, not a citation of Art. 73 (PhD-review finding 22).
provisions.evaluation_dsl_note: HONESTY CORRECTION (roborev/codex). The Art. 73 hard requirements — (1) at least one valid evidence path (public incident_card OR confidential card_source) carries public_incident_id + the trigger facts; (2) some coordinated_disclosure.regulatory_timeline[] entry has framework=='eu-ai-act-art73'; (3) that entry's stated deadline matches the shortest applicable clock (death->10 / 3.49.b|widespread->2 / else->15) — are ALL UNEXPRESSIBLE in the generic DSL: there is no rule-level OR/existential combinator across two record types, exists_where resolves a single RFC-6901 pointer per record and jsonpointer has NO array-wildcard (so no operator can scan order-insensitive array entries by a `framework` predicate), and no operator can COMPUTE a derived deadline. Encoding (1)/(2) as paired UNIVERSAL field_present rules is a FALSE GREEN: an empty bundle passes both vacuously, and field_present accepts an empty regulatory_timeline: []. Those vacuous field_present pairs (public_incident_id, regulatory_timeline on both paths) are therefore REMOVED and the enforcement is DELEGATED to the validator (F-M3-VALIDATOR-RULES, assertion VAL-CLOCK-001) per RFC-0002 §5.7 (line 270/278) and coordinated_disclosure.schema.json — see validator_delegated_enforcement below for the precise check list, fact-source paths, and ACEF-084. This provision retains ONLY rules the DSL CORRECTLY enforces, and both are ADVISORY (warning): an art73-notification-timeline-present check (notification_timeline[] is a per-incident_report POST-FILING record — the awareness->report->notification chain — so it is advisory, NOT fail-blocking: a confidential report built before submission legitimately has none and the exporter must not fabricate a notification_date; the CLOSED incident_card schema has no such field) and an advisory entity_linked. The BINDING Art.73 obligation (valid evidence path + stated deadline == shortest applicable clock) is the delegated ACEF-084 check, never these DSL rules — so the generic rollup for article-73 is SATISFIED whenever no fail-severity rule trips, and the fail-blocking enforcement lives in ACEF-084.

validator_delegated_enforcement.why_not_dsl: The generic ACEF rule DSL has no rule-level OR/existential combinator across two record types, no array-element scan (exists_where resolves a single RFC-6901 pointer per record; jsonpointer has no array-wildcard), and no derived-clock computation. Encoding these as universal field_present rules gives a false green (an empty bundle passes vacuously; an empty regulatory_timeline: [] is accepted).

checks.requirement: At least ONE valid evidence path exists carrying public_incident_id and the Art. 3(49) trigger facts (serious_incident_triggers[], widespread, death_involved): EITHER the public incident_card.taxonomy_crosswalk.eu_ai_act path OR the confidential incident_report.card_source.eu_ai_act_facts path (§5.7). A reserved-id, no-public-card confidential report is satisfied by the card_source path alone.
checks.reason: No DSL operator expresses an existential OR across two record types; paired universal field_present rules pass vacuously on an empty bundle (false green).

checks.requirement: Some coordinated_disclosure.regulatory_timeline[] entry has framework == 'eu-ai-act-art73' with an awareness_date and a deadline. The array is order-insensitive (§5.10); the matching entry MAY appear at any index. An empty regulatory_timeline: [] does NOT satisfy this.
checks.reason: exists_where resolves a single RFC-6901 pointer per record and jsonpointer has no array-wildcard, so no operator can scan order-insensitive array entries by a `framework` field predicate; field_present accepts an empty array.

checks.requirement: The matching eu-ai-act-art73 entry's stated deadline equals the shortest applicable clock computed over the trigger facts: death_involved -> 10 days; 3.49.b (critical infrastructure) OR widespread -> 2 days; else 15 days. The trigger facts are read from card_source.eu_ai_act_facts in confidential/source-backed validation and from taxonomy_crosswalk.eu_ai_act in public-card validation (§5.7). A mismatch raises ACEF-084.
checks.reason: No DSL operator can COMPUTE a derived deadline from the trigger array + modifiers and compare it to a stated deadline.

evaluation.message: An incident_report SHOULD carry a notification_timeline[] — the order-significant (§5.10) top-level incident_report field (incident_report.schema.json) recording the awareness->report->authority-notification chain. ADVISORY, not fail-blocking: notification_timeline is a POST-FILING record (it logs notifications that have OCCURRED), so a confidential Art.73 report constructed BEFORE submission legitimately has none yet, and an exporter MUST NOT fabricate a notification_date it does not have. The BINDING Art.73 obligation — the report exists on a valid evidence path and its stated deadline matches the shortest applicable clock — is enforced by the delegated validator (ACEF-084) over coordinated_disclosure.regulatory_timeline, not by this presence check; the CLOSED incident_card schema does not carry this field
Incident cards should link to the subject AI system whose serious incident is being reported

adoption.deferral_basis: Digital Omnibus draft postponement of the EU AI Act high-risk obligations (RFC-0002 §5.7 / Appendix E Q7). Until the amending Regulation is published in the OJ the as-enacted 2026-08-02 in-force date applies.

rules.description: Death of a person -> 10 days. Keyed on the death_involved fact, NOT the whole 3.49.a trigger (which also covers non-fatal serious-health-harm).
Serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure (3.49.b) OR a widespread infringement -> 2 days.

reporting_clock.default_description: Any other serious incident (including non-fatal 3.49.a serious-health-harm, 3.49.c non-widespread, 3.49.d property/environment) -> 15 days.
